title: The $P_5$-free coloring conjecture for prime non-bipartite cores
statement: Let $H$ be a graph. A **prime graph** is one admitting no non-trivial decomposition with respect to the direct product, a **core** is a graph with no homomorphism onto a proper subgraph, and a graph is **$P_5$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the path $P_5$. A **minimal obstruction to $H$-coloring** is a graph that does not admit a homomorphism to $H$, while every proper subgraph does. **$P_5$-free coloring conjecture.** If $H$ is a prime, non-bipartite core, then there is a finite family of minimal obstructions to $H$-coloring $P_5$-free graphs if and only if $H$ does not contain $C_4$ as a subgraph. The conjecture proposes a classification of when these minimal-obstruction families are finite; the paper notes that the corresponding behavior is already known for some odd cycles and cliques, but the general classification for prime targets remains open.
source_name: Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Karolina Okrasa, Paweł Rzążewski and Oliver Schaudt, “Minimal obstructions to C_5-coloring in hereditary graph classes”, arXiv:2404.11704 (2026).
